message: docs(adr): the severity parameter is deleted, the widening is gone, no raw literal remains

edits.find: `severity` is derived from the same record, through `ruleSeverity`, which is now the constructor's default in place of the literal `"error"` it used to be.
edits.replace: `severity` is derived from the same record, through `ruleSeverity`, which is now the only expression in the tree that answers the question rather than the constructor's default in place of the literal `"error"` it used to be.

edits.find: The parameter itself survives, and saying otherwise is the overclaim this record's own status paragraph exists to catch; it was said here once and is corrected in place rather than beside. A call site can still name a severity: `contract/validate-v5.ts` names one at several sites, `adapters/trigger-factory/default.ts` names one too, and `validate-v5.ts`'s own local helper still carries a `= "error"` default of its own one layer above the constructor, which is the same bug one level up and harmless today only because both keyframe warnings pass `"warning"` by hand. So this is a corrected default and not yet the invariant a reader might take it for. Deleting the parameter is owed, and what it is owed first is the compiler enumerating its call sites rather than a fourth hand count.
edits.replace: The parameter is deleted, and both of the corrections this paragraph has carried are recorded here in place rather than beside. It first claimed the invariant while only the default had moved, which is the overclaim this record's own status paragraph exists to catch; it then said the parameter survives, which was true when it was written and is not true now. Nineteen sites named a severity, every one named the severity its rule already fixes, so no diagnostic moved when the parameter went, and the compiler enumerating those sites is what the deletion was owed rather than a fourth hand count. `contract/validate-v5.ts` forwards a rule id, a path and a message and its own local helper carries no `= "error"` default any more, and `adapters/trigger-factory/default.ts` names no severity. There is no argument position left in which a call site could name one, so this is the invariant a reader might have taken it for, stated only now that it is true.

edits.find: and `graph-runtime.ts` `#report` all take `string` today, and a closed union whose only producer accepts `string` is closed nowhere.
edits.replace: and `graph-runtime.ts` `#report` all took `string` when this was written, and a closed union whose only producer accepts `string` is closed nowhere. All six take `RuleId` now, and the five that are not the constructor forward to it rather than building a frozen shape of their own, so the shape has one owner and the severity has one answer.

edits.find: There is no variant left to be checked against and no narrowing for an assertion to reach: with `Diagnostic` flat, `asDiagnostic` is a widening rather than a correlation stated once, so the "boundary stated rather than implied" this paragraph was written to describe stops describing a union. The widening survives only for the raw producers that still build a frozen object literal of their own, and it is deleted with the last of them. The assertion's own input is a separate question and the honest answer is that it is unchanged: `DiagnosticFields` keeps `ruleId` and `ids` independent, so a module calling `asDiagnostic` directly can still name a rule by a literal and hand over a payload it does not own. Three modules call it, all three are producers that derive their own list, and a fourth caller is the thing to refuse. This is therefore an assertion boundary rather than an invariant over every construction, and a record claiming otherwise would be the overclaim this paragraph exists to prevent.
edits.replace: There is no variant left to be checked against and no narrowing for an assertion to reach: with `Diagnostic` flat, `asDiagnostic` was a widening rather than a correlation stated once, so the "boundary stated rather than implied" this paragraph was written to describe stopped describing a union, and the widening was deleted with the last of the raw producers it survived for. `DiagnosticFields` went with it. That closes the hole this paragraph used to bound rather than merely bounding it: nothing can name a rule by a literal and hand over a payload it does not own, because no expression accepts the two independently any more. This is therefore an invariant over every construction rather than an assertion boundary, and it is stated only now that every construction goes through one call.

edits.find: What the compiler still cannot answer for is a producer forwarding a rule id it holds as data: `contract/validate-v5.ts` through `scopedRuleId`, whose two scopes are both idless, and `runtime/report.ts` through the private `frozenDiagnostic`, which is reached only from the exported member that now derives its own list. Those two are the widening's whole remaining subject, and both are backed by the record in `contract/rule.ts` rather than by a proof.
edits.replace: Two producers forward a rule id they hold as data rather than as a literal, and neither is an open question any more. `contract/validate-v5.ts` reaches the constructor through `scopedRuleId`, whose return type is narrowed to `KeyframeRuleId | ContributionRuleId`; every member of both families owns no ids, so the derived list is the empty one and the forwarding call is checked against it rather than accepted by a branch with no claim in it. `runtime/report.ts` reaches it through the private `frozenDiagnostic`, which is reached only from the exported member that derives its own list. The first is backed by the compiler and the second by the record in `contract/rule.ts`.

edits.find: was collapsed into the one constructor, while the equivalent producers in `runtime/report.ts`, `domain/plugins.ts` and `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` still hold both and are owed the same collapse, and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` was deleted.
edits.replace: was collapsed into the one constructor, the equivalent producers in `runtime/report.ts`, `domain/plugins.ts` and `domain/keyframe-compiler.ts` were collapsed after it, the four raw object literals in `graph/order.ts`, `graph/references.ts` and `runtime/graph-publisher.ts` were the last of the second ownership and forward through the constructor now, the `severity` parameter itself was deleted, and `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` was deleted. One further correctness question fell out of the ownership record rather than out of the rename: both deferred rules in `runtime/report.ts` answer `ids: "always"`, and `OwnedIds` proves that an argument was passed and never that it says anything, so a deferral was able to publish a warning whose payload named nothing. `DeferredSeeds` requires a seed list with at least one member, which makes that unrepresentable rather than merely unreached.
